title: High-Frequency Telemetry Ingestion
business: Financial services firms requiring microsecond-level data processing for market feeds.
problem: High-level managed languages introduce non-deterministic garbage collection pauses, causing significant data loss during market volatility spikes.
solution: Utilizing C++ allows for deterministic memory management and zero-overhead abstractions, ensuring consistent throughput for telemetry ingestion pipelines.
steps: Define fixed-size circular buffers to avoid dynamic memory allocation during the hot path.
Utilize stack-allocated structures to ensure cache locality and minimize pointer indirection.
Implement custom memory pools to manage object lifecycles without relying on the global heap.
Apply compile-time templates to generate specialized code paths for specific data packet types.
outcome: The system achieves stable, predictable latency profiles that remain consistent regardless of the volume of incoming market data.
limitation: Manual memory management increases the risk of memory leaks or dangling pointers; developers must verify safety using static analysis tools or modern RAII patterns.
